prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1006; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a side impact collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver side by a third-party vehicle that entered on a red signal, per initial statements. Police report requested. Photos of both vehicles received from insured. Claimant reported wrist fracture and was transported by ambulance from the scene.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained counsel. All further contact to be routed through the attorney's office per their letter of representation. Reviewed scene diagram and witness statement, which supports the third-party driver running the red light. Liability preliminarily assessed as clear against the other driver, pending police report confirmation.

Entry 3: Spoke with defense counsel's paralegal regarding the request for medical authorization. Authorization forms sent to claimant's attorney for signature. Orthopedic records indicate closed reduction of a distal radius fracture performed; follow-up scheduled. No recorded prior injury to the same wrist in claims history.

Entry 4: Vehicle inspection completed at the body shop. Damage consistent with a broadside impact to the driver door, B-pillar, and rear quarter panel. Supplement estimate requested for possible structural repair. Rental coverage confirmed for the insured while the vehicle is out of service.

Entry 5: Received demand package from claimant's attorney including medical bills and wage loss documentation. Currently under review. Requested the treating physician's narrative report and a current prognosis before evaluating the injury component. Reserve reviewed and flagged for supervisor discussion at next file review.
